scope: Controlled isolated Semantic Core 2.13 owned compatibility publication experiment; no default-authority, LOC, precise-provider or universal one-second qualification.
methodology: Six predeclared serial trials, three per frozen runtime. The control differs only by resolving every pending projection candidate instead of restricting unchanged owners to actual visibility transitions. Every trial retains complete support eligibility, navigation, membership, compatibility/query projections, FULL/WAL pointer commit and historical/GC/integrity checks. No required work is timed as pointer-only.
environmentLimitations: darwin arm64 Node v25.9.0; OS caches were not evicted; three samples per role are not p95 or a portable/cold-cache/power-loss guarantee. AC power and low-power mode 0 were observed in the original session, but raw power output was not included in these trial files. Compiler/provider RSS is not measured; these workloads launch no compiler.

evidence.scope: Synthetic owned compatibility graph publication, 100 edge shards and one high-fanout OR-of-AND support guard. This does not replace the original 1M SCIP occurrence/claim benchmark and is not LOC or producer qualification.

decision: Retain the visibility-transition optimization: the alternative-supported 100k-edge closure resolves 1 compatibility key instead of 100001, with a 395.456 ms versus 1089.285 ms median. Required core support closure still executes. First publication and actual 100k-edge deletion remain over one second. These synthetic graph projections do not replace the original 1M-occurrence/2M-claim SCIP benchmark.
